title: Contact deactivated after winning the claim, before the trip-end backstop runs
description: The identification is delivered live, at deliverAtSec 0, before any trip exists on this asset -- the contact is active at that moment, so any insert-time snapshot records it active. The scenario then deactivates driver A (external step, not part of this fixture) before the trip-end consumer ever runs. The trip's own frames arrive afterward as a full burst starting at burstStartAtSec 20. One HARDBRAKE at atSec 30, before the identification's claimed atSec 60, so it is a violation raised while the driver was still unknown -- this is the violation the `noTransfers: true` assertion depends on. Must prove: the identification consumer's insert-time snapshot is unaffected (still unlinked, no claim yet, since no trip existed at insert time), and the trip-end consumer's live re-check of the contact's enabled/deleted state (not the insert-time snapshot) is what actually blocks the award. Must NOT change: neither the asset assignee nor the trip assignee may ever move to A once the contact is deactivated, and no threshold event may be transferred.

events.note: violation while the driver is still unknown; noTransfers depends on this

driver_identifications.note: delivered before any trip exists; contact is active at resolution time. The scenario deactivates driver A afterward, before trip end, as an external step not encoded in this fixture
